title: Cognition Seeks $40 Billion Valuation Just Months After $1 Billion Raise
excerpt: The AI coding startup behind Devin is reportedly in talks with investors for a new funding round, powered by surging enterprise demand that could push its annualized revenue past $1 billion.
body:
• Cognition is reportedly in talks to raise a new round at a $40 billion valuation, according to Bloomberg
  • The company raised $1 billion at a $26 billion valuation just three months ago in May 2026
  • Enterprise revenue has surged from $492 million annualized run rate, with 50% month-over-month growth in usage
  • Major customers include Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, Dell Technologies, and the US Army

Cognition, the startup behind the autonomous AI coding agent Devin, is reportedly already in discussions to raise another funding round that would value the company at $40 billion or more, according to Bloomberg. The talks come barely three months after Cognition closed a $1 billion raise at a $26 billion valuation.

The potential new round would be contingent on Cognition achieving a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. That would represent a roughly doubling from the $492 million annualized revenue the company disclosed in May.

Rapid-Fire Growth

Cognition's trajectory has been one of the steepest in AI. The company, founded in August 2023 by former competitive programmers Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan — all International Olympiad in Informatics gold medalists — has seen its valuation climb from $350 million in early 2024 to $2 billion, then $4 billion, $10.2 billion, and $26 billion in successive rounds.

When Cognition announced its May funding round led by Lux Capital, General Catalyst, and 8VC, CEO Scott Wu told TechCrunch that enterprise usage of Devin had been growing 50% month-over-month for six consecutive months. The company counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, Santander, Dell Technologies, and branches of the US military among its customers.

The AI Coding Arms Race

The fundraise comes amid fierce competition in the AI coding tools market. Cursor, built by Anysphere, hit $2 billion in annual recurring revenue by February 2026 and has been the subject of a reported $60 billion acquisition deal. Anthropic's Claude Code has grown to more than $2.5 billion in run-rate revenue, while GitHub Copilot overhauled its pricing model in June, moving to usage-based billing.

Cognition has carved a distinct position by offering a fully autonomous agent rather than an AI-assisted development environment. Wu has emphasized that Devin is not sold as a human replacement — the agent typically handles long-tail grunt work that programmers often avoid, such as updating legacy software or migrating applications between platforms.

"Devin is often tasked with doing long-tail grunt-work that many programmers dislike, such as bringing old software up to date or moving applications off one platform and onto another."

— Scott Wu, CEO, Cognition

Windsurf Acquisition Paying Off

The company bolstered its product suite in July 2025 when it acquired Windsurf, an AI-powered IDE, after Google poached Windsurf's CEO and senior employees in a $2.4 billion acqui-hire deal. Cognition has since rebranded Windsurf as Devin Desktop, giving it both an autonomous agent and an integrated development environment to compete on multiple fronts.

Including the pending round, Cognition has raised over $2.5 billion to date. The company's May round drew participation from Founders Fund, Elad Gil, Ribbit Capital, Atreides, and Layer Global, among others.

What's Next

If the $40 billion valuation materializes, it would mark another near-doubling in just a few months and underscore how quickly investor appetite for AI coding infrastructure is growing. The key benchmark will be whether Cognition can convert its rapid enterprise adoption into the $1 billion revenue milestone that the new valuation reportedly hinges on.
